identity.intent: Make the living fuse the first tactical read through tactile workshop materials, physical non-hue state changes, distinct instrument verbs, and restrained cause-and-effect feedback while leaving screen composition open to implementation.

principles.statement: Fuse condition, threat direction, reach, target, health, and danger read before material ornament.
principles.rationale: The living fuse is a strategic object, not a background effect; decorative craft is useful only when it preserves decisions at normal gameplay scale.

principles.statement: Every thermal state changes silhouette, geometry, pattern, or attachment as well as color.
principles.rationale: STEADY, HOT, and FRAYED must remain distinguishable in grayscale, under reduced effects, and during dense combat.

principles.statement: Spark opens and recoils, Bell compresses and exhales, and Striker winds up and fractures.
principles.rationale: Strong silhouette and motion identities make reaction order readable without relying on color or long labels.

principles.statement: Cyan glass and the brightest cool light belong first to the heart, then to protection and cooling responses.
principles.rationale: A reserved focal material gives incoming threats a legible line of tension toward the game's consequence.

principles.statement: Use one readable anticipation-action-settle beat instead of high particle volume, large bloom, or constant shake.
principles.rationale: Physical cause and effect feels authored while preserving route and enemy readability and supporting reduced-motion play.

principles.statement: Tokens express roles and relative emphasis rather than fixed coordinates or a literal reference layout.
principles.rationale: Downstream implementers need a coherent language with room to solve the final Godot composition using engine-native evidence.

usage.warm: Action and danger; always pair danger with a notch, chevron, tab, or label.
usage.cool: Heart, cooling, protection, and keyboard focus; never flood the whole board.
usage.background: Lower saturation and contrast than route, threats, heart, and interactive affordances.

families.display: Humanist sans or restrained small-cap face with open counters.
families.interface: Clear sturdy sans with tabular numeral support.
families.fallback: Godot default sans when no project-bound font is available.

control.use: Short action verbs and instrument names

constraints.case: Sentence case for instruction; short uppercase only for compact mechanical states.

spacing.rule: Use relative grouping and breathing room; do not derive a fixed board grid from this scale.

shape.socket: Concentric round collar with a keyed notch; selection adds a second collar.
shape.danger: Downward iron chevron or sharp notch, never a soft badge alone.
shape.success: Seated collar, clean outward ring, or aligned seam.
shape.fracture: Three to five large wedges rather than confetti-sized shards.
shape.range: Thin authored arc with a material pattern; do not make range identity color-exclusive.

charredWalnut.value: Low-saturation grain with broad value variation.
charredWalnut.constraint: Subdue grain near tactical marks and essential text.

sootIron.value: Almost-black body with rough edge highlights.
sootIron.constraint: Use heavy silhouette for clamps, armor, disabled controls, and Striker.

hammeredBrass.value: Warm irregular rim with small value breaks.
hammeredBrass.constraint: Reserve brightest brass for active or available affordances.

copperFilament.value: Directional braid with a thin specular thread.
copperFilament.constraint: Expand for HOT and separate into branching strands for FRAYED.

boneCeramic.value: Pale crazed surface with a thick readable rim.
boneCeramic.constraint: Use for Cooling Bell and cooling collars, not general panel chrome.

cyanGlass.value: Internal light held by a visible metal cage.
cyanGlass.constraint: Heart first, cooling second; localized restrained bloom only.

waxAndSoot.constraint: Never overlap route, hit feedback, or labels.

material.lowEffectsRule: Material separation survives through base value and edge treatment when reflections, particles, and bloom are reduced.

screenShake.allowed: Boss clamp contact or break only

motion.rule: Use one dominant movement per beat and preserve the end-state geometry when motion is reduced.

events.waveIgnite: Short wax hiss into a low metal latch.
events.bellFire: Hollow ceramic tone with a cool breath tail.
events.strikerFire: Muted iron wind-up and weighted contact.
events.temper: Descending ceramic interval and steam release.
events.shatter: One sharp crack followed by two lower fragments.
events.flashboil: Compressed hiss then a tight pop, never an explosion wall.
events.leakCore: Cyan glass stress ping plus a low heart thump.
events.bossWarning: Two slow clamp knocks distinct from wave start.
events.victory: Resolved workshop chord with seated mechanism.
events.defeat: Extinguished filament decay with restart control unaffected.

mix.pitchVariation: Small variation only where instrument identity remains stable.
mix.reducedIntensity: Lower repeated high-frequency cues without removing semantic warnings.

waveReady: outline and enabled state become explicit

reactionStates.shatter: Broken ring or large fracture wedge.

accessibility.reducedMotion: Replace travel, shake, and particle bursts with held end-state geometry for at least 180 ms; simulation and timing windows do not change.
accessibility.reducedIntensity: Lower bloom, sparks, mist, shake, and repeated high-frequency audio without removing target, state, consequence, or action cues.
accessibility.grayscaleRequirement: Route state, instrument identity, threat direction, and available response remain readable without hue.

patterns.intent: Make one authored fuse band communicate shared tactical condition without becoming a secondary meter stack.
rules: Layer base shadow, physical sheath, conductive braid, one state attachment, and sparse local light.
Use a seated collar for STEADY, one raised tab for HOT, or one danger notch for FRAYED.
Keep the route continuous and more legible than environmental grain.
examples: A HOT bend widens its coil spacing and lifts one brass tab while the next STEADY band remains tightly braided.

patterns.intent: Keep Spark, Cooling Bell, and Striker recognizable by silhouette, material, and a single physical verb.
rules: Spark is tall and coiled with an opening shutter and narrow angular recoil.
Bell is wide and hollow with a thick ceramic rim, compression, and one low cooling ring.
Striker is squat and directional with a visible preload, contact face, and weighted recoil.
avoid: Same circular base with color swaps
Continuous idle particles as the identity
examples: At zero saturation, the coil, bowl, and offset hammer still identify the three instruments.

patterns.intent: Preview a concrete future interaction before the player commits economy.
rules: Seat a material-specific ghost above the socket and show one keyed alignment cue.
Show range geometry and the first reachable fuse band or target without promising a fixed target.
Confirm with a 60 ms seat and 140 ms collar settle.
avoid: Dense damage tables over the board
Large opaque range fills that hide the route
examples: A Bell ghost shows a ceramic rim, thin reach arc, and a cooling collar preview on the nearest reachable band.

patterns.intent: Connect the most imminent threat to the heart and the endangered route band without brightening every object.
rules: Place one forward iron chevron on the most imminent threat.
Pulse or notch only the threatened fuse band.
Keep the cyan heart luminous and environmental props subdued.
avoid: Full-screen red vignette for ordinary danger
examples: A Rivet Carrier approaching a FRAYED band receives one forward chevron while that band holds its iron notch.

patterns.intent: Make reaction order legible through instrument-specific cause and one physical consequence.
rules: Use anticipation, contact, one physical response, and settle.
Pair a compact reaction name or stable icon with the response.
Preserve route continuity and enemy health readability throughout the beat.
avoid: Generic burst motes for every reaction
examples: Temper seats a ceramic cinch and releases one low mist ring; Shatter replaces it with three fracture wedges and Striker recoil.

patterns.intent: Telegraph a single boss adaptation as a physical problem with a readable two-instrument response.
rules: Warn with two clamp knocks, a 140 ms iron jaw preload, and a marked target band.
Clamp contact creates FRAYED geometry and a visible jaw shield, never unexplained immunity.
Cooling adds a bone-ceramic collar and visibly loosens the jaw; Striker adds a fracture seam and breaks it.
avoid: Repeated clicking to loosen the clamp
examples: The clamp jaw changes from shut iron teeth to a cyan-rimmed loose gap before the Striker response becomes decisive.

patterns.intent: Make mouse and keyboard controls feel fitted to the workshop while remaining immediately discoverable.
rules: Use a deep walnut or soot face, fitted 5 px corners, a 1 px rim, and a 44 px minimum target.
Use a short action verb and explicit disabled or unaffordable treatment.
Give primary actions brass emphasis and keyboard focus a 3 px cyan exterior outline.
avoid: Using danger red for unaffordable state
examples: A ready wave-start plate warms its brass rim and steadies a small wick while the label remains readable.

patterns.intent: Close the run emotionally while keeping replay unambiguous.
rules: Victory reseats the fuse and heart cage with a controlled cyan and amber resolution.
Defeat extinguishes filament light while retaining readable heart silhouette and restart action.
Expose one obvious replay control with the same focus and pointer contracts.
avoid: Losing control contrast under ending overlays
examples: On defeat, copper falls to a dim edge rather than blacking out the control plate; restart receives the brass rim and cyan focus behavior.

references.role: Controlled material and fuse-state study for tactile construction, STEADY/HOT/FRAYED non-hue geometry, and instrument silhouette separation; not a final screenshot or layout.
references.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: controlled game visual-language study — material and fuse-state reference, not a final screenshot
Input images: Image 1 is the aspirational reference for tactile workshop materials, warm/cool lighting, and miniature craftsmanship; Image 2 is a baseline readability reference showing the existing single-route board and sparse silhouettes, not a layout to copy
Primary request: create one polished concept study for EMBERLINE showing a compact section of a living braided copper fuse across a charred walnut workbench, with three clearly separated physical state specimens: STEADY, HOT, and FRAYED. Integrate three small handcrafted instrument maquettes nearby: a copper-coil Spark instrument with a shuttered aperture, a crazed bone-ceramic Cooling Bell with a deep bowl, and a soot-black iron Striker with a heavy offset hammer. The study must establish reusable material and silhouette language, not dictate a full level composition.
Scene/backdrop: dark intimate workbench specimen stage with restrained iron fixtures, hammered brass collars, wax traces, and cool blue-black shadow
Style/medium: premium tactile miniature-diorama concept art; physically believable craft; painterly-real materials; code-native Godot implementation reference
Composition/framing: landscape 16:9, oblique top-down close study; three fuse-state specimens readable as a left-to-right progression; instruments separated with generous negative space; no complete game board and no HUD
Lighting/mood: precious ember warmth against cyan ceramic/glass cooling light; gently urgent, ingenious, slightly mysterious; controlled highlights, restrained bloom
Color palette: soot-black, charred walnut, ember copper, aged brass, bone ceramic, cyan glass; cyan reserved for heart/cooling/safe response and amber-red reserved for heat/danger
Materials/textures: braided copper, split sheath fibers, raised brass heat tab, dark iron danger notch, crazed ceramic, hammered brass, oxidized copper, soot, wax, glass
State communication: STEADY uses an intact tight braid and seated collar; HOT visibly expands the coil and raises one brass heat tab in addition to warmer light; FRAYED splits the sheath silhouette, exposes branching filament, and adds a sharp iron danger notch in addition to red-orange heat. The three states must remain distinguishable in grayscale.
Instrument identity: Spark reads tall and coiled with an opening shutter; Bell reads wide and hollow with a ceramic rim; Striker reads squat, weighted, and directional with visible recoil mechanics
Constraints: visual study only; no enemies, no characters, no medieval towers, no green terrain, no neon sci-fi, no glossy vector cards, no dense ornament, no interface mockup, no tiny labels, no logos, no watermark, no final-screen composition to copy

references.role: Controlled hierarchy, component, and motion study for placement, instrument beats, threat-to-heart direction, and the telegraphed Warden clamp response; not a final screenshot or layout.
references.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: controlled game visual-language study — gameplay hierarchy, reusable components, and motion beats, not a final screenshot
Input images: Image 1 is the aspirational reference for tactile workshop materials, warm/cool lighting, and miniature craftsmanship; Image 2 is a baseline combat-readability reference whose flat circles, uniform route, and sparse feedback must be materially surpassed without copying its layout
Primary request: create one polished EMBERLINE concept study arranged as four generous cinematic keyframe vignettes on a dark workshop presentation plate. Show how one living fuse, three handcrafted instruments, small coal-and-rivet threats, a luminous cyan glass heart, and one furnace-warden clamp communicate cause and effect at gameplay scale. The study should define hierarchy and motion signatures that can be rebuilt with Godot drawing and shaders, not prescribe a complete interface or level.
Scene/backdrop: oblique top-down miniature workbench fragments, each vignette focused on a short fuse bend with sparse physical props and controlled negative space
Style/medium: premium tactile miniature-diorama concept art; physically believable craft; painterly-real materials; code-native Godot implementation reference
Composition/framing: landscape 16:9 reference plate with four clearly separated vignettes and no complete board. Vignette 1: placement preview, an empty brass socket accepting a translucent instrument silhouette while a thin mechanical reach arc points to one fuse band. Vignette 2: instrument choreography, Spark shutter opens with a tight angular flare, Cooling Bell compresses then exhales one low ceramic-cinch mist ring, Striker winds up and snaps forward with three large fracture wedges. Vignette 3: threat hierarchy, two small enemies move along a HOT fuse toward a luminous cyan glass heart; the imminent threat has a forward iron chevron and the threatened segment has one raised tab, while background props remain subdued. Vignette 4: furnace-warden adaptation, a massive soot-iron clamp bites a FRAYED fuse segment; a cyan ceramic cooling collar visibly loosens the clamp, then a bold striker fracture seam shows the next response.
Lighting/mood: precious ember warmth against cool cyan heart and cooling accents; gently urgent, intimate, ingenious; strong focal falloff; restrained bloom and particle count
Color palette: soot-black, charred walnut, ember copper, aged brass, bone ceramic, cyan glass; cyan reserved for heart/cooling/safe response and amber-red reserved for heat/danger
Component language: primary actions use warm hammered-brass rims and deep walnut faces; selection uses a double mechanical collar; danger uses iron chevrons, raised tabs, split silhouette, and notches; cooling uses ceramic cinches and condensed rings; success uses a brief seated snap and clean outward ring
Motion language: anticipation 90–140 ms, action 60–100 ms, settle 140–220 ms; one dominant movement per beat; readable recoil and silhouette change; reduced-motion equivalents shown as held end-state geometry rather than particles
Accessibility: every important state must remain distinguishable in grayscale through silhouette, pattern, notch, collar, chevron, or fracture geometry; heart, threat, and available response form the brightest three-step hierarchy
Constraints: visual study only; no readable prose labels, no final HUD, no full game-screen composition, no floating magic runes, no generic medieval towers, no green terrain, no neon sci-fi, no glossy mobile cards, no particle fog, no tiny decoration, no logos, no watermark

metadata.hypothesis: A small physical fuse-state vocabulary plus instrument-specific silhouette and motion can expose local pressure and adaptation without a dense meter layer.
assumptions: The route remains the first gameplay read at 1152x720.
One local marker per fuse band is enough during combat.
Cyan can remain reserved for the heart, protection, cooling, and focus.
Downstream Godot rendering will interpret semantic roles rather than copy reference composition.
falsifiers: Fuse state needs a persistent legend during combat.
Bell becomes mandatory at every socket.
Particles or background material obscure route continuity.
State or instrument identity disappears in grayscale or reduced motion.
metadata.referencePolicy: The two ImageGen files are visual-language studies, not engine captures and not evidence of human enjoyment or final visual quality.
